sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.project_context:
<project_context>
Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/private/var/folders/24/2ff01nsx7cs9005l3jbptw8c0000gp/T/shallot-eval-falling-box-5HhuV3/app/AGENTS.md">
# Shallot project

Explore this project's entry, plugins and checks first; reuse its setup.

- Learn the API from the installed package, not memory. `bunx shallot create --help` lists the examples in `node_modules/@dylanebert/shallot/examples/`; start from the nearest one, its implementation and its checks, then the JSDoc in `node_modules/@dylanebert/shallot/src/` for the APIs it uses.
- Check your work as that example's checks do, with the cheapest evidence that answers: state, then a captured frame, then the browser.
- While you iterate, run only the check that answers your change: `bun test ./<file>` or `bunx playwright test <file>`. Before you finish, run `bun check` and `bun test` once; CI, `.github/workflows/test.yml`, runs every tier.
- `bun test` runs `*.test.ts` and `*.gpu.test.ts` only; run a `*.node.ts` check by path with `bun test ./<file>`. A full renderer or physics composition is a `tests/<goal>.node.ts` check, not a `*.gpu.test.ts`.
- `bunx shallot publish` builds, publishes to Cloudflare, or to itch.io with `--target itch`, and verifies the public game; read `bunx shallot publish --help` first. Commit its `package.json` destination and dependency changes. A first-link name collision refuses rather than overwrites; do not write `shallot.publish` by hand unless updating that Worker is explicitly intended. An itch.io page is created and set up by a person on itch.io; publish names the settings it cannot verify. A processed itch.io build awaiting a page view succeeds without interaction but is reported unverified; open the named page, then publish again to verify it.
- Cleanup, rollback and listing stay the provider's; `bunx shallot publish --help` names each command from the project's link. Confirm with the person before deleting a Worker or taking a page down: Wrangler's delete asks nothing without a TTY or in CI.
- Publishing without interaction needs the provider's credentials (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, plus `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` when ambiguous; butler's stored credentials or `BUTLER_API_KEY` for itch.io). CI's least Cloudflare token is custom, with Account → Workers Scripts → Edit on the one account; the "Edit Cloudflare Workers" template is broader. butler's login key has `wharf` scope, managing builds on every project the identity can reach, not one game; an account-settings API key can be broader still. Never put credentials in `package.json`. Publish adds no credentials to the build; Vite's client values, public files and source maps can still disclose what the project puts there. Never put secrets in them.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
# A box that drops and lands

I want a physics demo: a box starts up in the air, falls under gravity, and lands on a flat floor,
then comes to rest. Make the box a solid blue so it's easy to see, and give it a plain gray floor to
land on.

It should just play on its own when the project runs — no clicking needed.

  Options
    --template <example>  Copy an installed example
    -h, --help            Show this help

  Templates
    ambient-occlusion — Tune soft contact shadows where cubes meet and compare ambient occlusion quality costs.
    bloom — Shape HDR bloom around a bouncing grid of blue, white and red emissive spheres.
    city — A seeded city assembled from shared building parts, with an orbit and fly camera.
    color-grading — Shape HDR color-grading around a bouncing grid of blue, white and red emissive spheres.
    day-night-cycle — A sky, sun, shadows and haze follow a one-minute day; scrub the hour.
    embedded-scene — Embed a Shallot scene in an ordinary web page, with loading and rendering contained in its frame.
    first-person — Climb a first-person ascent with steps, a lift, and a block perch.
    hud — Svelte controls recolor a cube and set its turn speed, beside its live angle.
    interact — Aim at objects in a first-person room and use E to switch a lamp, press a button or hold to lift a block.
    isometric — A small isometric city with orthographic orbit, size zoom and bounded pitch.
    lit-interior — Walk a dark room between sunlight through a window and warm shadowed pendants.
    loading-screen — A game's own title card, held until its intro and minimum dwell end.
    low-res — Orbit a low-resolution diorama with nearest-filtered pixel-art crates, reduced colors and ordered dithering.
    materials — Orbit a gallery of plastic, metals, glass, textured wood, animated custom materials and banded lighting from an extended material.
    minimal — A turning cube and ground under an orbit camera, built with Shallot.
    minimap — Walk a cube arena with a top-down minimap and a player marker in a corner camera viewport.
    particles — Walk through GPU-simulated dust motes in a sunlit room and see their cost in the profiler.
    physics — Box3D samples in Shallot: stacking, joints, sensors, contacts and hit events.
    post-processing — Toggle lens distortion, chromatic aberration and vignette over a sunlit geometric gallery.
    save-and-load — Click a cube to build a coin pile, save it, and load it into the running game.
    snow-trails — Roll a boulder through deep snow and drag it to carve a persistent path.
    sound — Walk a first-person sound yard: moving spatial music, pause and resume, a synthesized chime.
    tonemapping — Shape HDR tonemapping around a bouncing grid of blue, white and red emissive spheres.
    view-model — A first-person view model that does not clip through walls, with independent FOV and shared lighting.
    volumetric-fog — Walk a dark hall through a shadowed sun shaft, a spot cone and point lamps glowing in fog.
    voxel — Scroll over seeded voxel hills with scattered grass, flowers, rocks and trees as GPU-meshed chunks stream into and out of view.
    world-ui — Follow a courier along a road with a world-space name, a progress bar, a line trail and an icon that scales away.

content.text:
The demo is built. When the page loads, a solid blue 1 m box drops from 5 m, lands on a plain gray floor and comes to rest. It starts without any clicking. You can still drag the camera around if you like.

**What changed**
- **`src/drop/index.ts`**: the new scene. The floor is a 10 × 10 m gray slab that doesn't move, with its top at height 0. The box starts at a height of 5 m and falls under the engine's default gravity. I made both lights plain white so they don't tint the floor; it renders at (159,159,159), a true gray.
- **`index.html`**: now runs this scene instead of the starter spinning cube. I also changed the page title to "falling box" and updated its description.
- **`src/welcome/`**: I deleted the starter scene and its test.

**Checks (all passing)**
- **`tests/falling-box.node.ts`**: runs the simulation and confirms three things:
  - the box falls more than 0.5 m in its first 30 steps;
  - it never sinks below 0.4 m;
  - it settles at 0.5 m (the box's center when it sits on the floor), and the physics engine reports it as asleep.
- **`src/drop/drop.test.ts`**: a quick check that the scene is set up as intended: a falling box held in the air above a fixed floor, blue box and neutral gray floor. Without it, `bun test` found no tests at all, which would fail CI.
- `bun check`, `bun test` and the browser startup tests (`bunx playwright test`) all pass.
- I looked at a screenshot of the running page after about 4 seconds: the blue box was resting flat on the gray floor, with a shadow. I didn't capture the box mid-fall in the browser, because the loading screen was still showing at the earlier screenshot. The fall itself is confirmed by the simulation test.

Run it with `bun run dev`.
